title: Your Work Story — Talking About Past Experience
description: Learn to tell your work history confidently using past tense verbs
objectives: Talk about jobs you had in the past
Say how long you did something using 'for' and 'from...to'
Use common irregular past tense verbs
Tell a short work history story

phrases: I have [X] years of experience in [field]
target_language.grammar_pattern:
PAST SIMPLE — Regular and Irregular
  Regular: work → worked, clean → cleaned, organize → organized
  Irregular: be → was/were, drive → drove, teach → taught, have → had

TIME EXPRESSIONS for past jobs
  I worked there for five years.
  I was a teacher from 2015 to 2020.
  I worked there until I came to the U.S.

USED TO
  I used to drive a truck. (I did this before, but not now)
  I used to live in Mogadishu.

grammar_patterns.label: Past Simple — regular verbs
examples: I worked at a warehouse for two years.
She cleaned offices every night.
He organized the stockroom.
I delivered packages across the city.

grammar_patterns.label: Past Simple — irregular verbs
examples: I drove a delivery truck for five years.
She taught English at a school.
He had a small restaurant.
I was a security guard from 2018 to 2022.

grammar_patterns.label: Time expressions with FOR and FROM...TO
examples: I worked there for three years.
I was a nurse from 2010 to 2019.
She worked at the restaurant for six months.
He drove trucks from 2014 until he moved here.

story.context: Ahmed visits a workforce center for help finding a job. A counselor, David, helps him talk about his work history in English.

dialogue.speaker: David
dialogue.text: Good morning, Ahmed. I'm going to help you today. Let's start with your work history. What was your job in Somalia?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: I worked as a delivery driver for five years. I drove a big truck every day.

dialogue.speaker: David
dialogue.text: Excellent. And before that? Did you have other jobs?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: Yes. Before I was a driver, I worked at a warehouse for two years. I organized the boxes and counted the inventory.

dialogue.speaker: David
dialogue.text: That's great experience. How do you say when you started and when you finished?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: I was a driver from 2017 to 2022. Then I came to the United States.

dialogue.speaker: David
dialogue.text: Perfect. Now, why did you leave your last job?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: I left because my family moved here. It was not a problem with the job. My employer liked my work.

dialogue.speaker: David
dialogue.text: That's important to say clearly. 'I left because my family moved to the U.S.' — that is a very good answer. What did you use to do there that you want to do here?

dialogue.speaker: Ahmed
dialogue.text: I used to drive every day, and I loved it. I want to be a driver again here. I have five years of experience.

dialogue.speaker: David
dialogue.text: You tell your story very well, Ahmed. That experience is valuable. Let's write it on your application.

drills.title: Regular Past Tense
drills.instruction: Change the verb to past tense. Use: I + [verb-ed]

prompts.sentence: I ___ at the warehouse for two years. (work)

examples: I worked as a cashier for one year.
She organized the office files.
He cleaned the restaurant every night.
I delivered packages to 50 houses a day.
We worked Monday to Friday, 8 to 5.
drills.your_turn: We worked Monday to Friday, 8 to 5.

drills.title: Irregular Past Tense
drills.instruction: Use the irregular past tense form of the verb.

prompts.sentence: I ___ a delivery truck for five years. (drive)
She ___ English at a primary school. (teach)
He ___ a security guard at a bank. (be)
I ___ a small business in my city. (have)

examples: I drove trucks from 2016 to 2021.
She was a nurse for eight years.
He taught math at a school in Mogadishu.
I had a job at a construction company.
We were co-workers for three years.
drills.your_turn: We were co-workers for three years.

drills.title: For, From...To, Until
drills.instruction: Complete the time expression. Use: for, from, to, or until.

prompts.sentence: I drove a truck ___ I moved here.
She worked at the hospital ___ six months.

examples: I worked there for four years.
I was a driver from 2017 to 2022.
She worked at the factory until she had a baby.
He cooked at the restaurant for two and a half years.
I worked from 7 AM to 4 PM every day.
drills.your_turn: I worked from 7 AM to 4 PM every day.

listening.question: How long did the woman work as a cashier?
listening.transcript: I worked as a cashier for two years, from 2019 to 2021.
listening.explanation: The woman says 'I worked as a cashier for two years, from 2019 to 2021.' The key time expression is 'for two years.'

listening.question: Why did the man leave his last job?
listening.transcript: Why did you leave your last job? I left because my family moved to a new city. It was not a problem at work.
options: He moved to a new city
listening.explanation: The man explains 'I left because my family moved to Portland. It was not a problem at work.' This is an important reason to explain clearly in an interview.

listening.question: What did the speaker used to do that she wants to do again?
listening.transcript: I used to teach young children in my country. I want to work with children here too.
options: She used to work at a hospital
She used to own a restaurant
She used to drive a school bus
listening.explanation: The speaker says 'I used to teach young children in my country. I want to work with children here too.' 'Used to' connects her past experience to her future goal.

speaking.title: Your Work History
speaking.instruction: Record yourself describing your work history. Include: what job you had, where you worked, how long you worked there, and why you left. If you have no work experience, describe a responsibility you had at home or in your community.
speaking.example: In my country, I worked as a cook at a small restaurant for three years. I cooked food and helped clean the kitchen. I left because I came to the United States with my family. Before that, I helped at a market for one year. I have four years of experience in food preparation.

speaking.title: Used To
speaking.instruction: Record 4 sentences about things you used to do in your home country that you want to do again here. Use: I used to...
speaking.example: I used to drive a truck every day. I used to work with a team of 10 people. I used to start work very early in the morning. I used to earn money to support my family. I want to do all of these things again here.

writing.title: My Work History Paragraph
writing.instruction: Write a paragraph (5-7 sentences) about your work experience. Include at least 3 different past tense verbs. Mention: what you did, where, how long, and what you learned.
writing.example: I have experience in transportation and warehousing. I worked as a delivery driver in Somalia for five years. I drove a large truck and delivered goods to many businesses. I also organized cargo in a warehouse for two years before that. I left my last job when my family moved to the United States. My employer wrote me a good reference because I was reliable and hardworking. I am looking for similar work here in Portland.

writing.title: From Past to Future
writing.instruction: Write 4 sentences connecting your past experience to what you want to do now. Use: I used to..., I have experience in..., I want to...
writing.example: I used to organize and manage a storage facility in Mogadishu. I have experience working with teams and following schedules. Now I want to find warehouse work in Portland. My past experience makes me a good worker for this kind of job.

sections.title: Regular vs Irregular past — there is no rule!
examples: work → worked ✓ (regular: add -ed)
clean → cleaned ✓ (regular: add -ed)
drive → drove ✗ NOT drived (irregular!)
teach → taught ✗ NOT teached (irregular!)
be → was/were ✗ NOT beed (irregular!)
have → had ✗ NOT haved (irregular!)
sections.question: Why do some verbs change completely in the past?
sections.explanation: English has many irregular past tense verbs. These must be memorized — there is no pattern. Common work verbs: drive→drove, teach→taught, have→had, be→was/were, make→made, come→came, sell→sold, build→built. Regular verbs simply add -ed: work→worked, organize→organized, deliver→delivered.

sections.title: USED TO — past habit, not present
examples: I used to drive a truck. (I drove before, but not now)
I drive a truck. (I drive now — present)
I drove a truck. (I drove at one specific past time)
I used to work nights. (My regular past habit)
She used to teach. (She was a teacher — no longer)
sections.question: When do we use 'used to' instead of simple past?
sections.explanation: 'Used to' is for habits or states that were true in the past but are NOT true now. It signals a contrast between then and now. 'I used to drive a truck' means: I drove trucks regularly in the past, but I do not drive trucks anymore (now I am here looking for work). It is very useful when talking to employers about your experience in your home country.

quiz.question: What is the past tense of DRIVE?
quiz.explanation: Drive is an irregular verb. Past simple: drove. 'I drove a truck for five years.' (Not 'drived' — that is a common mistake.)

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly uses 'for'?
options: I worked there for five years.
I worked there for until I left.
I worked there from five years.
quiz.explanation: 'For' is used with a duration (a period of time): for five years, for six months, for three days. 'From...to' is used with start and end dates: from 2015 to 2020.

quiz.question: Ahmed says 'I used to drive every day.' What does this mean?
options: He will drive every day in the future.
He drove every day in the past, but not anymore.
He wants to drive every day.
quiz.explanation: 'Used to' describes a past habit that no longer happens. Ahmed drove every day in Somalia. Now he is in the U.S. looking for work and does not currently drive professionally.

quiz.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: I was a driver from 2017 to 2022.
I was a driver from 2017 until 2022.
I was a driver for 2017 to 2022.
Both A and B are correct.
quiz.explanation: Both 'from 2017 to 2022' and 'from 2017 until 2022' are correct. You can use either 'to' or 'until' with 'from'. Both mean the same thing.

quiz.question: What is the past tense of TEACH?
quiz.explanation: Teach is an irregular verb. Past simple: taught. 'She taught English at a primary school for three years.'

quiz.question: How do you explain that you left a job because you moved to the U.S.?
options: I was fired because I moved.
I left because my family moved to the United States.
My company moved to the U.S.
quiz.explanation: 'I left because my family moved to the United States' is honest, clear, and easy for an employer to understand. It shows it was not a problem with your work or character.

quiz.question: What is the past tense of ORGANIZE?
quiz.explanation: Organize is a regular verb. Add -ed: organized. 'I organized the warehouse inventory for two years.'

quiz.question: What does 'I have five years of experience' mean?
options: I will work for five years
I worked for five years in the past
I have worked for five years and maybe more
Five years ago I started working
quiz.explanation: 'I have X years of experience' is present perfect in meaning — it covers your accumulated past experience. It is one of the most important phrases in any job conversation or application.

quiz.question: Write 3 sentences about a past job or responsibility using past tense verbs. Include 'for' or 'from...to' to say how long.
quiz.explanation: Practice your work story. Good format: what you did + where + how long. Example: I worked as a driver at a logistics company for four years.

quiz.question: An interviewer asks: 'Why did you leave your last job?' Write your answer in 2 sentences. Be honest and positive.
quiz.explanation: This is one of the most common interview questions. Keep your answer honest, brief, and positive. Never say anything negative about your previous employer.

somali.description: Baro sida taariikhda shaqadaada si kalsooni leh ugu sheegto falalka past tense
objectives: Ka hadal shaqooyinkii aad qabatay waagii hore
Sheeg inta aad wax qabanaysay adigoo isticmaalaya 'for' iyo 'from...to'
Isticmaal falalka past tense-ka caadiga ah ee aan qaanuunka lahayn
Sheeg sheeko gaaban oo taariikhda shaqadaada ah

sections.explanation: Ingiriisigu wuxuu leeyahay falal badan oo past tense ah oo aan qaanuun lahayn. Kuwan waa in la xafido — qaanuun ma jiro. Falalka shaqada ee caadiga ah: drive→drove, teach→taught, have→had, be→was/were, make→made, come→came, sell→sold, build→built. Falalka qaanuunka leh waxay ku daraan -ed keliya: work→worked, organize→organized, deliver→delivered.

'Used to' waxaa loo isticmaalaa caadooyin ama xaalado waagii hore run ahaa laakiin HADDA aan run ahayn. Waxay muujinaysaa isbeddel u dhexeeya waagaas iyo hadda. 'I used to drive a truck' waxay ka dhigan tahay: waagii hore si joogto ah ayaan gaadhi weyn u wadi jiray, laakiin hadda ma wado. Aad bay faa'iido u leedahay markaad shaqo-bixiyayaasha kala hadlayso khibraddaadii dalkaagii hooyo.
